sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (US-derived common law under the Compact of Free Association, Marshallese customary law, and statutory civil code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States (1986, as amended 2003)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus, signed 2017)
US-RMI Intergovernmental Agreement for FATCA Implementation (2014)
Tax Information Exchange Agreements with Australia and New Zealand (OECD Global Forum)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA), 48 MIRC Ch. 1, as amended, mandating share- and director-register maintenance; Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000 (FTRA), as amended, with subsidiary AML/CFT regulations, imposing CDD, UBO record-keeping, and suspicious-transaction reporting; Income Tax Act 1989, as amended, conferring Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) tax-exempt status on non-RMI-source income; Banks Act 1991 and Trust Companies Act 1992 (relevant only if licensed activity is added).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: RMI is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; documents are notarized, authenticated by the US Department of State if US-issued, then legalized by the Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands in Washington, D.C.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation (certified copies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (as above; RMI Foreign Service legalization of the Registrar's certification)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Consent to Act as Director/Officer and Shareholder register extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Notary Public (RMI/US) and Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by RMI consular legalization where the receiving bank requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Registrar certification plus RMI Embassy legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO/AML due diligence profile and corporate structure chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Registered Agent (FTRA-regulated company service provider)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registered agent's certified cover letter; notarization and consular legalization required only if the receiving institution demands it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) RMI domestic designations list; and (iv) international law-enforcement PEP databases. Risk-based approach under the FTRA requires fuzzy-match verification (similarity ratio >= 0.85) with manual review of all hits, enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs and sanctioned jurisdictions, and continuous monitoring aligned with the target payment rails (Alipay and SWIFT wire).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry - Office of the Registrar of Corporations (official filings made exclusively through licensed Registered Agents; the principal intermediary is International Registries, Inc. (IRI); no authoritative public name-search portal exists - a formal Name Reservation Application is submitted).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in the Latin (Roman) alphabet; English is the operative registry language. Non-Roman script names require a mandatory Latin transliteration in the Articles of Incorporation. Marshallese names must follow standard orthography; phonetically identical or confusingly similar names are deemed conflicts.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Marshall Islands (or RMI) where it implies official patronage
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant has 30 days to file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations through its licensed Registered Agent, attaching a fresh availability search and, for sensitive-token objections, the prior written consent of the Banking Commissioner or competent ministry. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may petition the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands for judicial review under the RMI Civil Procedure Rules within 90 days of the final administrative decision; no extension of the 90-day reservation is granted, but a new reservation may be re-filed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Title 51, Marshall Islands Revised Code 2006, as amended), Sections 27-30 (Articles of Incorporation, filing and effect), Section 34 (consideration for shares), Section 38 (registered agent), Section 45 (officers) and Section 52 (bylaws); the Act is modeled substantially on the Delaware General Corporation Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (BCA Form 1) with accompanying Statement of Acceptance of Registered Agent (BCA Form 1A), filed pursuant to Title 51, Sections 27-28.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; BCA Section 34 permits shares to be issued for any consideration fixed by the board of directors. The pro-forma first resolution establishes 1,000 issued shares at $1.00 par value, producing $1,000 stated capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts its Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations and approves the issuance of 1,000 shares of Common Stock, $1.00 par value, to the subscriber under the subscription agreement for $1,000, receipt of which is acknowledged.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be maintained at the office of the Corporation's licensed registered agent in Majuro, Marshall Islands, which agent is authorized to accept service of process.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary/Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to execute all documents, open bank accounts, and effect ancillary registrations necessary for the Corporation's B2B e-commerce operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General (electronic filing via the Marshall Islands Business Registry portal, Majuro).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application listing three proposed corporate names in descending priority. The Registrar conducts a conflict search against the corporate names database and, if available, reserves the approved name for sixty (60) days. Pay the USD 50 reservation fee by wire transfer or bank card; in-person submissions may use a US-dollar bank draft.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Notarized evidence of applicant identification (passport or corporate identity document)
Name search and reservation fee remittance (USD 50)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on grounds of identical or deceptively similar conflict, file an amended application designating the next-ranked name; no additional fee is charged within the same submission window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Incorporation in duplicate, stating the corporate name, the registered agent and office, the authorized share structure, and the incorporator's signature. Attach the registered agent's signed Statement of Acceptance and file both with the Registrar together with the USD 187 filing fee. Standard processing is five to seven business days; a two-hour expedited service is available for an additional USD 150.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (BCA Form 1), executed in duplicate
Statement of Acceptance of Registered Agent (BCA Form 1A)
Certificate of Name Reservation
Consent to Act as Director of each initial director
Consent to Act as Officer of each initial officer
Filing fee remittance (USD 187)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency or query notice, submit a Certificate of Correction under BCA Section 28(6) within twenty (20) days; alternatively, amend and refile the Articles. The paid filing fee is applied to the first successful refiling within the same fiscal quarter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent approved by the Business Registry Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent in Majuro to maintain the statutory registered office and to accept service of process on behalf of the corporation. Execute the agency agreement, obtain the physical addresses of the agent and registered office, and, if the agent named in the Articles is replaced, file a notice of change of registered agent.
required_dossiers: Registered agency engagement agreement
Statement of Acceptance by registered agent
Proof of physical registered office address in Majuro
Certificate of Incorporation (to be placed in the registered agent's corporate kit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent ceases to be licensed, the Registrar will notify the corporation; the corporation must appoint a successor agent within thirty (30) days or face administrative dissolution. A change of agent is effected by filing the BCA Change of Registered Agent form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Action and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sole incorporator and initial board of directors (internal corporate governance act).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole incorporator executes a written consent adopting the bylaws, designating the initial directors, and ratifying the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments as set forth in the pro-forma resolution. The Secretary is directed to issue share certificate No. 1 for 1,000 shares to the subscriber and to open the stock ledger reflecting the subscription.
required_dossiers: Written consent of the sole incorporator
Adoption of Bylaws (executed minutes or unanimous written consent)
First board resolution (pro-forma text incorporated by reference)
Share certificate No. 1 for 1,000 shares of Common Stock
Initial stock ledger entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective or incomplete governance act may be ratified by a subsequent unanimous written consent of the directors or an ad hoc board meeting; no court intervention is required for intra-corporate curative resolutions under BCA Section 52.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Confirmations, Tax Status Verification, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General; Marshall Islands Tax Administration (Ministry of Finance); licensed international banking institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a Certificate of Good Standing from the Business Registry to evidence due incorporation and standing. Obtain a tax-status confirmation from the Ministry of Finance that the non-resident Business Corporation is outside the Gross Revenue Tax net because it derives no Marshall Islands-source income (or, if locally registered, a Business Privilege Tax exemption certificate). Present the corporate kit to an international bank to open a USD corporate account enabling Swift Wire and Alibaba Pay settlement rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certificate of Good Standing
Articles of Incorporation and bylaws
First board resolution and share certificate copy
Government-issued photo identification of officers
Tax status confirmation letter (as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, supplement with a board resolution ratifying the account opening and a current Certificate of Good Standing; if the tax authority issues an adverse determination, appeal to the Minister of Finance within thirty (30) days of the ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Investment and the Foreign Investment Board of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (conditional authority only; no industrial license is mandated for a purely digital offshore B2B marketplace).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing license is required for the non-resident B2B e-commerce platform. If a physical presence is later established within the Republic, a General Business License under the Business License Act 1990 and, where foreign ownership exceeds the local threshold, a Foreign Investment Business License under the Foreign Investment Business Act would become conditionally mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 (Registration / Exempt): no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required for a pure-play B2B digital marketplace with no manufacturing plant, no wastewater discharge process, and no atmospheric emission source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge thresholds apply to the digital platform itself. If a staffed office is opened in Majuro, the premises must connect to municipal sewer or a licensed septic system, with sanitary effluent meeting EPA National Water Quality Standards (BOD ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L); administrative operations generate no VOCs or combustion emissions; end-of-life IT equipment must be reused or recycled through an EPA-approved e-waste take-back program under the Solid Waste Management Regulations 2013.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety, structural load, or occupational clearance is required for a virtual foreign-zone operation without local physical premises. If a Majuro office is staffed, a Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Majuro Fire Department and an Occupational Safety and Health workplace compliance assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2016 must be obtained prior to occupancy, together with a structural soundness certificate issued by the Municipal Building Inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance, Tax and Revenue Division (Majuro); official portal: RMI Tax and Revenue Office electronic services at www.rmi-finance.org and paper filing at the Ministry of Finance, Majuro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The RMI does not maintain a general VAT or income TIN system applicable to foreign non-resident entities. A non-resident Business Corporation without RMI-source activity or a place of business in the RMI is not required to register. If an RMI tax nexus is created (e.g., physical place of business, employer obligations, or RMI-source gross revenue), the entity must submit the Business License Application (Form BL-1) and Taxpayer Registration (Form T-1) to the Ministry of Finance, attaching the certificate of incorporation, registered agent consent, and corporate resolutions. The Ministry then issues a Business License Number and, where applicable, a Withholding Tax Account Number. No VAT ID exists under RMI law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The RMI Income Tax Act imposes no check-the-box partnership, disregarded-entity, or hybrid mismatch elections. A non-resident Business Corporation is statutorily classified as a foreign corporation taxed only on gross revenue derived from sources within the RMI under the Gross Revenue Tax regime; income from foreign cross-border e-commerce, including B2B marketplace commissions and software/platform fees, is outside RMI tax jurisdiction. No election is required to achieve this result, and no hybrid mismatch election exists in RMI legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - the RMI imposes no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax. The only transaction-adjacent tax is the Gross Revenue Tax under the Income Tax Act 1989 (currently 3% on gross revenue sourced in the RMI) and import customs duties under the RMI Customs Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST - no such tax exists. For RMI Business License purposes, a license fee becomes due upon maintaining a place of business or undertaking business activities within the RMI; there is no de minimis turnover threshold for license registration, but a non-resident pure online B2B marketplace with no RMI physical presence or RMI-source revenue has no registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI has no real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoice clearance API, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate. Invoicing is governed by general commercial practices; in practice, the RMI Tax and Revenue Office may request local paper or PDF records during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because the RMI does not levy VAT/GST, there is no 0% export VAT rate or export refund mechanism. A non-resident BC's cross-border B2B services and goods sold through the marketplace are outside the scope of RMI gross revenue tax provided the sale is not sourced in the RMI (title, risk, and place of performance outside the RMI).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable - RMI imposes no VAT export zero-rating or input VAT refund regime; no customs export documentation bundle is required for tax refund purposes. Entities should, however, retain export declarations, bills of lading, airway bills, invoices, payment confirmations, and written contracts to evidence foreign-source income and the absence of RMI-source revenue.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export zero-rating VAT exists, so no VAT clawback or fraudulent zero-rating penalty regime applies. General anti-avoidance scrutiny nonetheless applies: mischaracterization of RMI-source gross revenue as foreign-source (e.g., digital services delivered to RMI-based customers or payments routed through a foreign platform while economic activity occurs in the RMI) may trigger reassessment under the Income Tax Act 1989, late payment interest of 1.5% per month, a late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, license suspension under the Business License Act 1990, and, for willful tax evasion, criminal fines and potential revocation of the business license. No currency repatriation deadline exists; the RMI uses the U.S. dollar and imposes no exchange controls.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not operate a domestic central bank and has adopted the United States dollar as its sole legal tender. As a result, there is no foreign exchange control authority, no independent monetary policy, and no distinction between capital-account and current-account convertibility. Profit remittances and capital repatriations are unrestricted at the sovereign level; however, banks and trust companies are subject to anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) obligations under the Marshall Islands Banking Act and related regulations, and may require satisfactory source-of-funds and economic-substance documentation before processing outward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to any central bank or government agency, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Exporters may freely retain, hold, or disburse USD-denominated proceeds. Nevertheless, licensed banking institutions may apply internal compliance policy requiring documentary evidence of the underlying trade transaction—such as invoices, bills of lading, or platform transaction reports—to support the credit of export receipt and to comply with correspondent banking due diligence expectations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low—no offshore electronic money institution (EMI) or digital payment service is licensed by the Bank of Guam or Bank of the Marshall Islands for the purpose of providing domestic banking services to non-resident corporate clients, and the Marshall Islands Banking Act does not recognize non-resident EMI banking licences. Offshore digital EMIs generally cannot clear USD payments locally and would require a correspondent banking arrangement through a US or foreign bank to execute SWIFT transactions. Such EMIs may be used only as auxiliary payment gateways for the B2B marketplace, with a licensed Marshall Islands commercial bank remaining the primary clearing and settlement entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Marshall Islands AML/CFT regulations and the account-opening policies of licensed commercial banks, directors and authorized signatories are not statutorily required to appear physically for every account opening; remote onboarding is permitted where the bank is satisfied with enhanced due diligence. However, a bank may, at its discretion, require a physical visit or in-person video interview when the applicant is a non-resident business corporation, the beneficial owners are located in high-risk jurisdictions, or the proposed transaction volumes exceed the bank's internal threshold. In all cases, a notarized certificate of incumbency, board resolution, and source-of-funds declaration must be supplied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership is a B2B marketplace structure with cross-border platform flows and multiple non-resident beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate registry extraction from the Republic of the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations showing the legal entity chain to ultimate individuals; an operating agreement or service agreement defining the marketplace role; a compliance manual proving transaction monitoring for trade counterparty verification; and affidavit of source of funds for each contributing shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions originate from or are destined to countries with weak AML regimes or countries subject to Financial Action Task Force (FATF) statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A financial crime risk rating matrix covering all active marketplaces and payment corridors; a territorial screening policy that marks restricted counterparties; copies of licenses or registration certificates for users in affected jurisdictions; and evidence of asset-freeze or negative-news screening performed before onboarding of each merchant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds through the operating account involving low-margin, high-volume electronic wholesale trades
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed payment-flow diagram identifying buyer, seller, platform, and settlement accounts; a detailed transaction ledger for the latest twelve months showing linkage between trade records and wire instructions; duplicate/impairment controls preventing commingling; and an auditor-reviewed reconciliation policy for unallocated payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are executed in United States dollars via international wire transfer from the investor's bank through the SWIFT network, typically a MT103 message to the receiving Marshall Islands commercial bank's correspondent in the United States (often a US Federal Reserve member bank). The receiving bank will request the sender to include the company's account number and the purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION', accompanied by a board resolution and share subscription documents. The bank will verify the source of funds before crediting the account; where the funding exceeds a specified threshold, a formal source-of-funds questionnaire and certified ownership records must be provided.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for interbank transfers, with a USD-denominated commercial letter of credit (LC) used where the buyer or seller requires documentary protection. For lower-value marketplace disbursements, banks in the Marshall Islands may also support automated clearing house (ACH) or Fedwire transfers to US bank accounts. The seller's invoice, shipping documents, and applicable purpose code such as 'REMITTANCE FOR IMPORTS' or 'TRADE PAYMENT' must be attached to the remittance order; all wires are subject to OFAC screening and correspondent-bank restrictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged with a licensed offshore bank or broker, permitted because the Marshall Islands has no domestic currency and no restrictions on offshore hedging
Plain-vanilla foreign currency forwards involving USD vs a trade counterparty's currency, settled through the international interbank market

Cross-currency interest rate swaps executed for term-liquidity hedging under an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement, with Marshall Islands banking law imposing no prudential restriction on qualified non-resident corporations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Annual Return) and Franchise Tax - US$750 baseline (authorized capital up to US$50,000; higher fees apply on the statutory sliding scale above US$50,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar rule: due on or before 31 October of each year, not tied to the incorporation anniversary; the Registrar invoices from 1 September and a late-remittance window runs to 30 November
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge applied to remittances received after the statutory deadline; continued non-payment allows the Registrar to administratively dissolve or strike off the corporation after notice, without court proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Retention and Continuity Declaration (a non-resident corporation must at all times maintain a licensed RMI registered agent and registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed RMI Registered Agent (the agent files its own annual license renewal with the Registrar; the company executes the annual engagement and consent forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, submitted concurrently with the 31 October corporate renewal cycle; continuation of the agent appointment is a precondition to acceptance of the annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the registered agent appointment voids the registered office; failure to appoint a successor agent within the Registrar's cure period is a ground for administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (AML/CFT) Record Refresh and Annual Confirmation to the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RMI Registered Agent (AML/CFT gatekeeper under the RMI Registered Agents Act and AML/CFT Regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual refresh at the 31 October renewal cycle and within 30 days of any change in shareholding or ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm blocks the annual renewal and may require the agent to file a suspicious-transaction report with the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; a false declaration is an offence subject to fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a non-resident, tax-exempt Business Corporation: the Business Corporations Act does not require appointment of an auditor, preparation of audited financial statements, or filing of accounts with the Registrar; an audit becomes mandatory only through bank/lender covenants, commercial agreements, or voluntary resolution of the board or shareholders
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutorily prescribed accounting framework for non-resident BCs; IFRS is the market-standard basis for any voluntarily prepared or externally required financial statements, with US GAAP equally acceptable for US-financed operations; internal management accounts may be maintained on any consistent basis

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RMI maintains no public beneficial-ownership register and no UBO return is filed with the Registrar. At each annual renewal the licensed registered agent must secure a signed officer/owner confirmation that the register of members and UBO schedule are current and unchanged; any share transfer requires immediate update of the register of members and a refreshed UBO declaration to the agent within 30 days of the transfer, together with supporting KYC documents for any new beneficial owner
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register) - maintained at the RMI registered office or the registered agent's records center
Minute book of shareholder and director proceedings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 1,500 per annum (prevailing market range for a non-resident BC, exclusive of the US$750 government fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 per engagement (voluntary certified audit for a small B2B marketplace entity; no statutory audit is required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 3% on gross income derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI Income Tax Act 1989, s.154(a)); effective rate 0% for this Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) holding an exemption certificate under the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Act 2019 (metadata classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: NRDC exemption certificate: 0% income tax, 0% gross revenue tax on foreign-source income; no capital gains tax, no estate or gift tax, no payroll tax, no stamp duty, no exchange controls; annual NRDC certification fee payable to the Registrar. Net operating loss carryforward of 5 years is available for non-exempt corporations only; an exempt NRDC has no RMI taxable base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (ITA Form CR-1, generic R-200 series) filed with the Division of Revenue and Taxation (DRT), Ministry of Finance; e-filing through the DRT taxpayer portal with paper attestation for audit trail. Exempt NRDCs are not required to file Form CR-1; they must file the annual Economic Substance Return (Form ESR-01) and the annual NRDC declaration (Form NRDC-D1) with the Registrar of Corporations via the MIRC e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the taxable year; the standard RMI taxable year runs 1 October to 30 September, so the statutory due date is 31 December. The Commissioner may grant a 6-month extension upon written request; corporate returns cannot be extended past the later of 30 June or the date 9 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: RMI tax identification number, legal name, MIRC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the NRDC registration number and exemption certificate reference; state that no RMI-source activity is conducted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address and registered agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the licensed RMI registered agent address; this is the address for service of process and DRT correspondence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature of business and principal activity classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120: cross-border B2B electronic wholesale marketplace operation; add 'no RMI-situs commercial activity'

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from sources within the Republic
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 if all platform revenue is earned from non-RMI counterparties; RMI-source income is taxable at 3%

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from sources outside the Republic (exempt foreign-source income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter total foreign-source gross income; attach a schedule of counterparty jurisdictions and platform fee composition

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax at 3% on Line 4, credits, and net remittance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt NRDC: enter 0; attach the NRDC Act 2019 exemption certificate issued by the Registrar

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature of director or authorized officer; place and date of signing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sign under penalty of perjury; ensure the declaration is consistent with the ESR return and beneficial ownership filings

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of a corporate return: US$1,000 flat penalty plus US$100 for each month of continuing default; statutory interest at 0.5% per month on unremitted tax. Failure to file the annual ESR return triggers separate penalties of up to US$20,000 initially and US$10,000 per month of continuing default. Fraudulent filing or willful evasion is a criminal offense under ITA s.165 with fines up to US$5,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends declared by a Marshall Islands Business Corporation, regardless of the shareholder's residence or the source of the profits distributed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has not entered any comprehensive double tax agreement; the only tax arrangement with the United States (2003) covers international shipping and aircraft income and does not govern dividend repatriation. Accordingly, no DTA relief form or Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) submission is required from the RMI payer side. Where the shareholder's home jurisdiction requires evidence of RMI tax status, the DRT will issue a certificate of tax status on application; such certificate confirms 0% RMI withholding and does not constitute an exemption from the shareholder's domestic income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties: 0%. Statutory withholding tax on interest: 0%. Treaty rate under the US shipping arrangement: 0%. No domestic tax is imposed on outbound payments of IP royalties or debt interest; no RMI registration or prior approval for such payments is required.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 - the RMI has not enacted a Local File or Master File documentation regime, and there is no statutory monetary threshold requiring transfer pricing documentation. ITA s.105 nevertheless empowers the Commissioner to allocate, apportion, or adjust gross income and deductions among related taxpayers where the pricing does not reflect an arm's-length result. Exempt NRDCs must maintain contemporaneous economic substance evidence (board minutes, payroll records, lease and utility contracts, bank statements) demonstrating management and physical presence in the RMI for ESR purposes.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations 2019 (as amended 2021), administered by the Registrar of Corporations, apply to all entities registered under the Business Corporations Act. A cross-border B2B electronic marketplace deriving income from related-party transactions is classified as a 'Distribution and Service Centre' / 'Provision of Services' relevant activity and must satisfy the economic substance test: (i) management and control exercised in the RMI (at least 2 board meetings per year held in the RMI, with original minutes maintained), (ii) physical premises in the RMI, (iii) adequate number of qualified local employees, and (iv) adequate local operating expenditure proportionate to the income. An annual ESR return is mandatory. An entity claiming tax residence in another jurisdiction must file a non-resident exclusion claim supported by a foreign tax residence certificate issued by a non-blacklisted jurisdiction; failure to qualify for exclusion triggers full national substance requirements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Failure / Shell Company Determination
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Rendering related-party marketplace or distribution services while maintaining no physical office, no employees, and no expenditure in the RMI; filing a false ESR return or failing to file the annual ESR return for a claiming entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the ESR Regulations 2019: initial penalty up to US$20,000; continuing default penalty of US$10,000 per month; repeat default triggers involuntary strike-off by the Registrar and referral to the Commissioner of Revenue for asset recovery and collection of unpaid fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false substance declarations are personally liable for civil restitution of exemptions and fees obtained; penalties up to US$10,000 and imprisonment up to 1 year; travel bans, revocation of RMI business registration, and disqualification from acting as a director may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating RMI-source gross income, forging or misusing the NRDC exemption certificate, concealing beneficial ownership through layered entities, or routing transactions through the B2B marketplace to artificially shift profits to the RMI exempt zone.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA 1989 s.165: criminal misdemeanor, fine up to US$5,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; additional civil fraud penalty of 50% of the tax evaded; the DRT may issue jeopardy assessments, freeze bank accounts, and enforce tax liens against settlement balances held through Alibaba Pay or Swift Wire rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where fraud is proven; directors, officers, and controlling shareholders are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution to the DRT, personal fines, passport revocation, travel bans, and extradition under the RMI Extradition Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding client funds, operating an escrow or payment settlement function, or conducting money transmission through Alibaba Pay / Swift Wire rails without a license from the Banking Commission; failure to maintain AML/CFT policies, customer due diligence, and Suspicious Transaction Reports under the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Banking Act 1991: fine up to US$25,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for unlicensed banking or money service activity; the Banking Commission may impose asset freeze orders, suspend settlement accounts, and prohibit the marketplace from processing payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for gross negligence in AML oversight; orders may include personal asset freezes, travel bans, disqualification from managing any regulated financial business, and criminal prosecution of the responsible compliance officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Compliance with NRDC Exemption and Registrar Obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent, failure to file the annual NRDC declaration (Form NRDC-D1), non-payment of annual registration or certification fees, or conducting domestic RMI business while holding an NRDC exemption certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Business Corporations Act: involuntary dissolution and strike-off from the MIRC registry; restoration fee of US$100 per month of default plus all outstanding fees; upon dissolution, undistributed assets escheat to the Republic; violations of the NRDC Act 2019 carry fines up to US$10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: After strike-off, directors are personally liable for corporate debts arising post-dissolution; the corporate veil is pierced upon a finding of misrepresentation to the Registrar, subjecting directors and officers to civil restitution, criminal fines, imprisonment, and travel restrictions pending resolution.
